title: The Best Lugia Cards to Collect — Neo Genesis to the 30th Celebration, Raw to PSA 10, Dated Sold Prices | Gengar's Collector's Desk
description: Gengar's pick of the Lugia cards that are true collectibles: Neo Genesis Lugia (1st Edition and Unlimited), the Aquapolis Crystal Lugia, the Neo Revelation rare, the 30th Celebration Lugia #149, the Team Up Lugia and an under-$25 shelf — each with dated raw, PSA 9, PSA 10 and TAG 10 sold prices and eBay links.
keywords: best lugia cards, lugia cards to collect, neo genesis lugia, crystal lugia aquapolis, lugia 30th celebration, most valuable lugia cards, lugia card collection
intro: Lugia has fewer cards than the other giants and a higher share of them matter. The Neo Genesis holo is one of the great vintage cards full stop, the Aquapolis Crystal is a six-figure slab, and this year's 30th Celebration Lugia is the heaviest card in that whole set. A short desk, on purpose.
narratorNote: A shorter list than Charizard's, and I'd rather that than pad it. Every number is a dated sold price from our own index data, every print is searched by its exact set and number. One Lugia I can't price yet is named below so you know the hole is mine, not the card's.

shelves.label: The grails
shelves.blurb: Two Wizards-era Lugias. Both are notoriously hard grades, and the PSA 10 column shows it.

entries.title: Neo Genesis Lugia #9 (2000)
entries.why: The first Lugia card, the holo from the first Neo set, and one of the hardest vintage cards to find in a 10: Neo Genesis print quality was poor enough that gem copies are famous for being scarce. Our ladder has no PSA 10 mark for either print because clean title-verified 10 sales simply have not come through at the rate our rule needs. The 1st Edition is the serious print; the Unlimited is the collector's way to own the art.

entries.title: Crystal Lugia, Aquapolis #149 (2003)
entries.why: One of the Aquapolis Crystal Pokémon secret rares, from the second-to-last Wizards set. It is the heaviest card in our Aquapolis index and trades mostly graded, which is why the raw mark rests on only a handful of sales.

shelves.label: The centerpieces
shelves.blurb: The Lugias with a clear chase slot in their set and enough sales to mark.

entries.title: Lugia #149, 30th Celebration (2026)
entries.why: The top card of the 30th Celebration set by weight in our index, released this September. Too new for a graded mark that meets our rule; the raw column is the one to read for now, and the TAG column is the one grader with enough early sales to show.

entries.title: Lugia #20, Neo Revelation (2001)
entries.why: The second Wizards-era Lugia, a rare from Neo Revelation. Nowhere near the Neo Genesis card in price, which is exactly why a collector who wants a vintage Lugia on the shelf starts here.

entries.title: Lugia #131, Team Up (2019)
entries.why: The Team Up Lugia, a $20 raw card whose PSA 10 sells for many multiples of that — the sign of a card that was pulled, played and sleeved late. A cheap way into a graded Lugia set.

entries.title: Lugia V alternate art, Silver Tempest (2022)
entries.why: The modern Lugia everyone chases is the Silver Tempest alternate-art Lugia V, and it is the one card on this desk I can't put a number on: we don't track Silver Tempest yet, and I won't print a price I can't point at on our own pages. It belongs on this list, so it is on this list — with a search instead of a mark.

collectingNotes.h: Why the Neo Genesis 10 column is empty
collectingNotes.p: Our graded marks require at least three title-verified sales in 30 days or two in 90. Neo Genesis Lugia PSA 10s trade so rarely that neither print met that bar at the last read, so the ladder shows no mark rather than a number we can't stand behind. The PSA 9 column is the one with a real market on it.

collectingNotes.h: 1st Edition and Unlimited are different cards
collectingNotes.p: Neo Genesis and Neo Revelation each exist as a 1st Edition print and an Unlimited print with separate PSA labels, separate population reports and separate price histories. Our indices track them separately and every link on this page searches for the exact print on the row.

The Silver Tempest Lugia V alternate art is named above without a price because we do not track that set yet. When it enters our data it gets a ladder like the rest; until then it gets a search link and an honest blank.

PSA 10 is the hobby's price reference. TAG grades by machine-measured imaging with human review and publishes a full defect report for every card, which is why we link TAG slabs beside PSA on every row. We think measured grading is where the hobby is heading — our view, not a price claim. How TAG grading works →
